subject: Nimbus SLO test plan and hosted vs incumbent latency probe

Subject: Post-call: latency targets & streaming profile

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope a hosted vs incumbent qualification run: 

Summary of targets (end-to-end, client -> app -> Redwood/incumbent -> client):
- p95 target: <= 120 ms
- p99 target: <= 350 ms
- Typical response size: 300–1,200 tokens (median ~520)
- Throughput expectation: steady 600 req/s, peak bursts up to 1.2k req/s for ~3–5 minutes
- Concurrency: sustained ~200 active connections, spikes to ~400 during peak windows
- Streaming: chunk latency budget <= 50 ms between consecutive tokens/chunks; we use server-sent-chunk model with partial JSON framing

What we can provide: traffic profile + sample payloads (attached: nimbus-traffic-profile.csv).
What we need from Redwood:
1) Proposed SLO test plan and measurement criteria (how you define client-side end-to-end p95/p99).
2) A test harness or endpoint to run a side-by-side probe vs our incumbent provider. Ideally we’ll do the same scripts against both to minimize instrumentation differences.
3) Clarify any header-level instrumentation you need (trace ids, timestamps) so we can correlate logs.

Timeline: we’re aiming to get a quick smoke by Jan 20 and a full run Jan 21–22.

Open to a short runbook or checklist from your side to ensure we capture identical scenarios.

Attachments: nimbus-traffic-profile.csv (CSV, 1.2 MB)

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: Post-call: latency targets & streaming profile — measurement notes

Priya / Marissa — a few technical notes so the measurement is apples-to-apples. Please see inline.

Measurement definition (client-observed):
- Start timestamp: time request bytes first sent from client socket
- End timestamp: time last byte of final payload is received by the client and fully flushed to the application (not just socket ACK).
- For streaming, we measure per-chunk delta (time between chunk arrival to client process). We will compute p95/p99 both on per-chunk latency and full response completion latency.

Sampling and stability:
- Use full-span tracing for 1% of requests to validate correlation integrity; aggregate timing for 100% of requests using client-side timestamps.
- When we report p95/p99, we’ll publish both the raw values and the 95% confidence interval computed from bootstrapped samples so you can see variance between runs.

Probe guidance (attached script stub: slo_probe_script.sh):
- Run the exact same script and traffic profile against both endpoints (incumbent and Redwood-hosted). Don’t use any synthetic client-side delay; only the traffic CSV-driven request distribution.
- For concurrency, open persistent connections to simulate real client behavior — avoid new TCP handshakes per request if your product does persistent HTTP/2 or WebSocket connections.

A/B considerations:
- If we run both providers from the same test origin, ensure network egress path is the same (same NAT/IGW) to avoid asymmetric network differences. If that’s not possible, run mirrored probes from two identical origins and compare.

I’ll upload the probe stub to the shared Drive and include a short runbook for running the container.

Attachments referenced: slo_probe_script.sh (text, 3 KB)

Thanks,

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the docs and the measurement notes. Confirming the following so we can kick off the runs tomorrow morning: 

Confirmed inputs:
- Traffic file: using nimbus-traffic-profile.csv (we’ve validated token buckets and adjusted client-side batching).
- Client origin: both probes will run from our GCP project (same NAT egress) to minimize network differences.
- Warm-cache behavior: we have a per-session KV cache (TTL 30m). For the run, we’ll disable client-side warm caches for parity and rely on server-side prefix caching only.
- Streaming: we’ll run a separate streaming-only pass and a combined pass.

Acceptance bar (for us to consider Redwood hosted for initial rollout):
- p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 350 ms in the steady-state 30-minute window
- No functional errors above 0.2% (4xx/5xx) during steady-state
- Chunk latency distribution: per-chunk p95 <= 50 ms

We approve the probing schedule for Jan 21–22; please proceed with the runs you manage and share raw CSV outputs and a short summary table for each provider. HubSpot updated with our intent to proceed (HS-987654).

Attachments: none included in this reply.

Best,
